stories.title: Bank of Canada likely to hold policy rate steady in December after flat October CPI
stories.summary: Statistics Canada reported that the consumer price index for October rose 3.1 % year‑over‑year, unchanged from September and driven mainly by high energy prices. Economists cited the data as indicating that inflation is not spreading beyond energy costs and said it raises the likelihood that the Bank of Canada will keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged at its December 9 meeting. The central bank had raised the policy rate in October, its first hike since July 2023.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.

stories.title: Russia says biggest Ukrainian drone attack hits Crimea bridge, minor damage
stories.summary: Russia reported its largest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, saying a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained only minor damage. The Russian military said it intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four Flamingo long‑range missiles over 24 hours, with about 600 drones directed toward Moscow. Kyiv experienced a record 17 air‑raid alerts and blackouts affected roughly 50,000 people.
stories.why: The event highlights the escalating intensity of the conflict and the vulnerability of critical Russian infrastructure.

stories.title: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem to step down in June 2027
stories.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem announced he will not seek a second term and will leave office when his seven‑year term ends on June 2, 2027. The central bank has started a search for his successor and aims to complete the appointment by the spring of 2027. Macklem, 65, said his tenure involved guiding Canada through a fragmented, shock‑prone world.
stories.why: A change in the Bank of Canada’s leadership can affect monetary‑policy direction and market expectations.

stories.title: Estonia to close road border crossings with Russia from Dec 1
stories.summary: Estonia announced it will shut all road border crossings into Russia on 1 December, saying Moscow was behind an attempted arson at a drone‑manufacturing plant north of Tallinn. Prime Minister Kristen Michal described the Saturday break‑in, in which suspects used flammable liquids, as part of Russia’s broader hybrid war. Local media say the arrested suspects are Latvian.
stories.why: The closures will affect cross‑border trade and raise security tensions in the region.

stories.title: Indian government bond yields rise on fresh inflation data and rate‑hike expectations
stories.summary: Indian government bonds fell as selling pressure increased amid fears of imminent interest‑rate hikes. The benchmark bond yield climbed slightly, mirroring movements in U.S. Treasuries. Fresh inflation data has sharpened market expectations that both the U.S. Federal Reserve and the Reserve Bank of India may raise rates, leading analysts to revise their inflation outlook ahead of the RBI’s next meeting.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.

stories.title: OpenAI adds CSAM image classifier and ChatGPT warnings
stories.summary: OpenAI introduced an image classifier, built with the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children and offered free via API to select partners, that in early testing cut flagged images by 48% while maintaining detection of abusive content and made flagged images twice as likely to be truly abusive. ChatGPT now displays warning screens for prompts that sexualize children, provides support resources, and imposes a 24‑hour account suspension for violations, with repeated offenses potentially leading to permanent removal.
stories.why: The tools aim to reduce the spread of illegal child sexual content and protect users and reviewers from exposure.

stories.title: Warren Buffett donates $5.47 billion of Berkshire Hathaway Class B shares to charities
stories.summary: Warren Buffett announced a donation of about $5.47 billion in Berkshire Hathaway Class B shares, amounting to 9,225,000 shares, to four charitable foundations. The donation brings his cumulative giving of Berkshire stock to over $29 billion. He continues to own roughly 13% of Berkshire and expressed confidence in the company’s leadership.
stories.why: The sizable transfer may influence investor sentiment and underscores Buffett’s continued support for Berkshire’s management.

stories.title: U.S. prepares interim rule tightening AI chip export controls
stories.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department announced an interim rule that will require licenses for any export, reexport, or transfer of AI chips and server hardware to data centers worldwide if the equipment could be used to provide compute to entities in China or other countries on the D:5 embargo list, which includes Russia, Iran, North Korea and 18 others. The rule expands existing controls that already mandate licenses for direct shipments of AI chips to those jurisdictions, aiming to block remote access to U.S. AI infrastructure.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.

stories.title: Rupee rises 0.3% to 93.9225 as November equity inflows near $10 billion
stories.summary: The Indian rupee closed 0.3% higher at 93.9225 per dollar, buoyed by foreign equity inflows of almost $10 billion in November that reversed recent outflows. Analysts said the inflows helped stabilize the currency amid expectations of possible U.S. interest‑rate hikes. The Nifty 50 index also rose 0.6%, supported by limited exposure to AI‑related trades.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.
